chapters.1: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' growing faith and endurance under persecution, assuring them that God will one day repay their persecutors and give them rest when Jesus returns in judgment. He prays that God would make them worthy of their calling and bring glory to Christ through their lives.
chapters.2: Paul corrects a false idea that the day of the Lord had already come, explaining that first there must be a rebellion against God and the appearance of a lawless figure who exalts himself as God, currently held back but destined to be destroyed when Christ returns. He thanks God that the Thessalonians were chosen for salvation and urges them to hold firmly to what he taught them.
chapters.3: Paul asks for prayer for himself and his co-workers and expresses confidence that the Thessalonians will keep following his instructions. He addresses believers who had stopped working and were idly meddling in others' affairs, commanding them to work quietly for their own bread, and tells the church to lovingly correct anyone who refuses, while still treating them as a brother.
